newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil says CVRD find won't affect sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says CVRD find won't affect sale.

text.p: Presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral said reports of a new gold and copper find would not affect the selloff of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), but would add to the company's price.
Amaral told reporters at his daily briefing that a report in the O Estado de Sao Paulo daily claiming CVRD had made a "historic" new find was old news.

"The research carried out by CVRD (in this area) will not affect the privatization, but merely add to the value," he said, adding that prospective buyers of CVRD already had full access to information on the find in the company's dataroom.

Earlier, CVRD contested the Estado story, explaining that it was still too early to evaluate the mineral content of deposits in Carajas, Para state, near the the existing Igarape Bahia gold mine and the Salobo gold, copper and silver project.
Planning Minister Antonio Kandir reaffirmed the government's intention to kick off the CVRD privatization in the first quarter of 1997.
Brazil's National Privatization Council is due to meet January 29 and will discuss the CVRD privatization, possibly setting firm dates for the sale.
